cues.zh: 这是一个珀尔帖元件。
cues.en: This is a Peltier element.

cues.zh: 它看起来可能只是一块不起眼的材料，
cues.en: It may look like a rather unassuming hunk of material,

cues.zh: 但在这两块板之间，夹着一大堆精心排列的半导体结，它们能做出一些了不起的事情：
cues.en: but sandwiched between these two plates are a whole bunch of semiconductor junctions that have been carefully arranged to do something remarkable:

cues.zh: 当我在两根导线上施加直流电压时，这块板就会变冷。
cues.en: when I apply a DC voltage across these two wires, the plate becomes cold.

cues.zh: 这被称为热电制冷，它的实现要归功于珀尔帖效应。
cues.en: This is called thermoelectric cooling, and it’s happening thanks to the Peltier effect.

cues.zh: 随着制造工艺的进步，我们现在能够快速且廉价地生产这些器件。
cues.en: With advances in manufacturing, we are now able to produce these devices quickly and cheaply.

cues.zh: 这里的这些每个成本不到3美元。
cues.en: These ones here cost less than $3 each.

cues.zh: 这项技术只有一个小问题：
cues.en: There’s just one little issue with this technology:

cues.zh: 它不太好用。
cues.en: it’s not very good.

cues.zh: 应该说，完全不好用。
cues.en: Like, at all.

cues.zh: 好吧，我们需要先交代一些背景。
cues.en: OK, we’re gonna need some context.

cues.zh: 我做这个视频有几个原因：
cues.en: I’m making this video for a couple of reasons:

cues.zh: 首先，你可能知道我唯一的真爱——制冷循环。
cues.en: First, you may know about my one true love, the refrigeration cycle.

cues.zh: 我超爱好的热泵，能跟你聊上好几个小时停不下来，
cues.en: I adore a good heat pump and could talk your ear off about them for hours on end,

cues.zh: 但基于蒸汽压缩的制冷系统笨重且机械结构复杂。
cues.en: but vapor-compression based refrigeration systems are bulky and mechanically complex affairs.

cues.zh: 它们还因为所用制冷剂而存在一些环境问题。
cues.en: They also have some environmental issues stemming from the refrigerants they use.

cues.zh: 正因为这些缺点，每隔一阵子——规律得简直能拿来对表——
cues.en: Because of those downsides, with a regularity you could practically set a watch to

cues.zh: 总有善意的人发现珀尔帖元件，然后质疑我们为什么不用它。
cues.en: well-meaning people discover Peltier elements and question why we don’t use these instead.

cues.zh: 一个没有活动部件、只要给它通电就能制冷的装置，确实很有未来感！
cues.en: A device with no moving parts and which makes cooling happen simply by putting voltage across it does feel like the future!

cues.zh: 那肯定比我们造冰箱的那一堆麻烦事强多了，对吧？
cues.en: That’s gotta be better than all the faff we go through to build a fridge, right?

cues.zh: 嗯，“更好”这个词可不好说。
cues.en: Well, “better” is a slippery word.

cues.zh: 首先，珀尔帖元件得名于让·夏尔·阿塔纳斯·珀尔帖，他在1834年就发现了这个现象。
cues.en: For one thing, the Peltier these are named for is Jean Charles Athanase Peltier, and he discovered this phenomenon back in 1834.

cues.zh: 我们在这方面尝试了很久，但它仍然没能改变世界。
cues.en: We’ve been taking cracks at this for a long time, yet it still hasn’t changed the world.

cues.zh: 确实，这种冷却方式有一些独特的优势
cues.en: It is true that this form of cooling offers some unique advantages

cues.zh: 在非常特定的应用场景中，配合同样特定的设计约束，使用帕尔贴元件是有一定道理的。
cues.en: and in very specific applications with equally specific design constraints, using a Peltier element can make some sense.

cues.zh: 然而，真正适合使用它们的情况非常非常罕见。
cues.en: However, the situations in which these are truly appropriate to use are very, very rare.

cues.zh: 看到最后你一定会明白为什么会这样，但现在（这也引出了我做这个视频的第二个原因）
cues.en: You will absolutely understand why that is by the end, but for now (and this leads into the second reason I’m making this video)

cues.zh: 你应该知道，如今在售的大多数使用这类东西的产品
cues.en: you should know that the majority of products on sale today which use these things

cues.zh: 纯粹是在利用我们就是忍不住买便宜垃圾货这一点来赚钱。
cues.en: are being made purely to capitalize on the fact that we just can’t stop ourselves from buying cheap crap.

cues.zh: 说到便宜垃圾货，你以前可能见过这些小型的个人冰箱。
cues.en: Speaking of cheap crap, you’ve probably seen these little personal refrigerators before.

cues.zh: 这样你就能在桌上冰几罐你最爱的饮料了！
cues.en: The idea is you can keep a few cans of your favorite beverage cool on your desk!

cues.zh: 你绝对会成为办公室的话题人物！
cues.en: You’ll be the talk of the office, for sure!

cues.zh: 这些东西都用帕尔贴元件来冷却内部，原因很简单：
cues.en: All of these things use Peltier elements to cool their insides for a very simple reason:

cues.zh: 成本。
cues.en: cost.

cues.zh: 它们必须足够便宜，人们才会冲动购买。
cues.en: These have to be cheap enough for people to pick them up impulsively.

cues.zh: 确实便宜——这个只要30多美元。
cues.en: And they are - this was priced just over $30.

cues.zh: 你没法用这么低的成本造一台像样的冰箱，但你可以造一个小塑料盒子，里面装个廉价电源和2美元的帕尔贴模块。
cues.en: You can’t build a proper fridge that cheaply, but you can build a little plastic box with a cheap power supply and $2 Peltier module in it.

cues.zh: 而且人们会买。
cues.en: And people will buy it.

cues.zh: 你看，我也是人，我就买了！
cues.en: Look, I’m a people, and I bought it!

cues.zh: 但它好用吗？
cues.en: But is it any good?

cues.zh: 剧透预警：
cues.en: Spoiler alert:

cues.zh: 不好用！
cues.en: No!

cues.zh: 让我们打开它，好好测试一番！
cues.en: Let’s turn it on and put it through its paces!

cues.zh: 它有个电源开关，贴心标着“关”和“冷”。
cues.en: It has a power switch helpfully labeled “Off” and “Cold.”

cues.zh: 这就是品质的象征，没错。
cues.en: That's a sign of quality, that is.

cues.zh: 来吧，试试看！
cues.en: Here goes nothing!

cues.zh: [风扇转起来] 哦，它居然还有内部照明！真贴心。
cues.en: [a fan spins up] Ooh, it’s even got an interior light! How thoughtful.

cues.zh: 但是，呃，对于一个没有活动部件的家伙来说，这噪音也太大了吧。
cues.en: But, uh, that’s a lot of noise for something with no moving parts.

cues.zh: 怎么回事？
cues.en: What gives?

cues.zh: 嗯，帕尔贴元件本身没有任何活动部件，但一开始我给你们展示的时候，只展示了一面。
cues.en: Well, the Peltier element itself doesn’t have any moving parts but when I showed you it in the beginning, I only showed one side of it.

cues.zh: 那一面确实在变冷，而在这个……所谓的冰箱里，元件的冷面粘在后壁上
cues.en: That side was getting cold, yes, and in this... alleged fridge the cold side of the element is bonded to the rear wall

cues.zh: 从热像仪里可以看到它在变冷。
cues.en: which we can see getting cold in the thermal camera.

cues.zh: 但帕尔贴元件在一面产生制冷的同时，元件的另一面会变热。
cues.en: But as the peltier element generates cooling on the one side, the other side of the element gets hot.

cues.zh: 非常热。
cues.en: Very hot.

cues.zh: 热得有问题。
cues.en: Problematically hot.

cues.zh: 为什么呢？有两个原因。
cues.en: Why? Well, two reasons.

cues.zh: 帕尔贴模块通过吸收冷面的热量，并将其穿过元件移动到热面来产生制冷。
cues.en: Peltier modules produce cooling by absorbing heat on the cold side and moving it through the element to the hot side.

cues.zh: 所有冷却都是这个原理——能量不会凭空消失，所以要降低某个位置的热能，
cues.en: That’s how all cooling works - energy doesn’t just disappear, so to lower the amount of heat energy in one location,

cues.zh: 就得从那里吸收热量，再转移到别处。
cues.en: you have to absorb it from that location and move it somewhere else.

cues.zh: 这些器件正是这么做的。
cues.en: Which is exactly what these do.

cues.zh: 它们在这面吸热（对我们来说就是变冷），在热面放热。
cues.en: They absorb heat on this side (which to us feels like coldness) and reject it on the hot side.

cues.zh: 但热量只是穿过一层质量极小的薄屏障，所以很快就积攒起来。
cues.en: But since the heat is only moving across a thin little barrier with very little mass, it builds up really quickly.

cues.zh: 还不止如此！
cues.en: But that’s not all!

cues.zh: 元件本身运行时也会发热。
cues.en: The element itself creates heat as it runs.

cues.zh: 这些额定是12伏5安，满负荷运行时会在很小的空间里耗散60瓦的热量，
cues.en: These here are rated 5 amps at 12 volts, so when running at full capacity they’re dissipating 60 watts of heat in a really small space,

cues.zh: 这还不算它从冷面吸来的热量。
cues.en: and that’s on top of the heat it’s pulling from the cold side.

cues.zh: 所以为了防止它把自己烧坏，需要在热面贴一个鳍片散热器把热量散开，
cues.en: So, to keep it from destroying itself, you need a finned heat sink bonded to the hot side to spread that heat out,

cues.zh: 还需要一个风扇把空气吹过散热器，让热量散得更快。
cues.en: and you’ll also need a fan to force air across the heat sink to spread the heat even more quicklier.

cues.zh: 如我们所见，这个迷你冰箱背面挂着一个相当大尺寸的散热器，还有风扇直吹。
cues.en: And as we can see here, the itty bitty fridge has a generously sized heat sink hanging off the back with a fan blowing right at it.

cues.zh: 风扇加散热器的组合并不复杂也不昂贵，但这意味着噪音比你预期的要大，而且，你知道的，多了一个活动部件。
cues.en: A fan and heat sink pair isn’t complicated or expensive, but it means this is noisier than you might expect and, ya know, adds a moving part.

cues.zh: 但噪音尚可原谅，真正的问题是它的效果如何？
cues.en: But noise is forgivable, the real question is how well does it work?

cues.zh: 这个问题的答案是：不行！
cues.en: And the answer to that question is: not!

cues.zh: 从你能想到的每一个指标来看都是如此。
cues.en: And by every conceivable metric you can imagine.

cues.zh: 首先，你可能注意到了，它没有温度设置。
cues.en: For a start, you may have noticed this has no temperature settings.

cues.zh: 要么制冷，要么关闭。
cues.en: It’s just cold or off.

cues.zh: 这是因为它只承诺将内部温度降至比环境温度低最多30度。
cues.en: That’s because it only promises to lower the internal temperature by up to 30 degrees below ambient temperature.

cues.zh: 仅此而已。
cues.en: That’s it.

cues.zh: 我欣赏它的坦诚，但如果你对食品安全有所了解，现在肯定会感到不安。
cues.en: I appreciate its honesty, but if you know anything about food safety, you’re gonna be getting the willies right now.

cues.zh: 因为在夏天办公环境里，比如说室温可能达到华氏75度，
cues.en: Because in an office environment during the summertime where, say, the room temperature might be 75 degrees Fahrenheit,

cues.zh: 这东西最多也就把内部降到华氏45度，按美国标准这达不到食品安全温度。
cues.en: this thing will - at best - get the interior down to 45 degrees Fahrenheit which by US standards is not food safe.

cues.zh: 所以……第一分丢掉了。
cues.en: So… strike one.

cues.zh: 但好吧，假设你只是想冰几罐饮料，不在乎食物。
cues.en: But ok, let’s say you just want to cool some beverages and you don’t care about food.

cues.zh: 为了看它效果如何，我把它塞满了6罐常温饮料，
cues.en: Well, to see how well it manages that I loaded it up fully with 6 room temperature beverage cans

cues.zh: 然后在它们之间的空隙里塞了一个温度数据记录仪。
cues.en: then shoved one of my temperature data loggers in the void space between them.

cues.zh: 运行两小时后，里面甚至还没降到华氏60度以下。
cues.en: After running for two hours, it hadn’t even gotten below 60 degrees inside here.

cues.zh: 12小时后，它才勉强降到华氏48度，
cues.en: After 12 hours it had only managed to drop to 48 degrees Fahrenheit,

cues.zh: 24小时后，温度在46度左右趋于平稳。
cues.en: and after 24 hours the temperature had plateaued at about 46 degrees.

cues.zh: 不太行。
cues.en: Not very impressive.

cues.zh: 不知怎么的，快到24小时的时候它又回光返照了一下，
cues.en: Somehow it got a bit of a second wind right near the 24 hour mark,

cues.zh: 我觉得这应该是因为它所在的房间稍微凉快了一点，
cues.en: which I believe happened just because the room it was in had cooled off a little,

cues.zh: 最后最低降到了45.5度。
cues.en: and we ended up bottoming out at 45.5 degrees.

cues.zh: 公平地说，这比室温低了大约30度。
cues.en: Which, in fairness, was about 30 degrees below the room temperature.

cues.zh: 所以它确实做到了它说的那样，但花的时间实在太久了。
cues.en: So it did what it said it would, but it sure took ages to get there.

cues.zh: 不过，我测的是冰箱正中间的空气温度，而罐子都贴着内壁，
cues.en: However, I was measuring the air temperature in the center of the fridge and since the cans are all touching the sides,

cues.zh: 结果发现罐子里液体的实际温度稍微高一点，是50度。
cues.en: I found that the actual temperature of the liquid in those cans was a slightly warmer 50 degrees.

cues.zh: 算是凉了吧，但这么温的啤酒我可不想喝。
cues.en: Chilled, I suppose, but I wouldn’t want a beer that warm.

cues.zh: 所以……第二次失败。
cues.en: So… strike two.

cues.zh: 不过好吧，严格来说它不算冰箱，
cues.en: But okay, so it’s not technically a refrigerator

cues.zh: 降温要花一辈子，
cues.en: and it takes forever to cool down

cues.zh: 也保不了那么冷，
cues.en: and it doesn’t keep things that cold

cues.zh: 而且比包装上暗示的要吵，
cues.en: and it’s louder than the box implies

cues.zh: 但这不代表它没用！
cues.en: but that doesn’t mean it’s not useful!

cues.zh: 这个嘛，严格来说你也没错！
cues.en: And to that I’d say, you’re not technically wrong!

cues.zh: 有些人用这东西把某些化妆品放在阴凉干燥的地方，据我所知他们还挺满意！
cues.en: Some people use these things to keep certain cosmetic items in a cool, dry place, and from what I can tell they’re happy to have these!

cues.zh: 如果50度对你来说够冷了，而且你勤快地轮换罐子进出，
cues.en: And if 50 degrees is cold enough for you, and you’re diligent about rotating cans in and out,

cues.zh: 你或许还真能把它当饮料冷藏箱用。
cues.en: you might actually enjoy this as a beverage cooler.

cues.zh: 但第三击来了，而且很致命
cues.en: But here comes strike three, and it’s a doozy

cues.zh: （这也是为什么帕尔贴器件通常很糟糕）。
cues.en: (and also why Peltier devices are generally terrible).

cues.zh: 如果你多少在意这东西干活干得不怎么样还费多少电，
cues.en: If you’re at all concerned with how much energy this thing will use to do its job not very well,

cues.zh: 你该知道这东西一直消耗约55瓦的功率。
cues.en: you should know that this thing consumes about 55 watts of power all the time.

cues.zh: 这功率不算大，没错，但你猜什么比它更省电？
cues.en: That’s not a ton of power, no, but guess what uses less power than that?

cues.zh: 嗯，很多东西，但跟这次讨论最相关的是——
cues.en: Well, lots of things but most relevant to this discussion -

cues.zh: 一台真正的冰箱。
cues.en: an actual refrigerator.

cues.zh: 这就是我所说的标准方块冰箱，市面上能买到的最基础的小冰箱。
cues.en: This here is what I call the standard cube fridge, the most basic mini-fridge you can buy.

cues.zh: 它们一般卖100美元左右，虽然极其简陋，但确实是真正的冰箱。
cues.en: They’re generally around $100 and while they are incredibly basic they are also actual refrigerators.

cues.zh: 后面有个小小的压缩机，让制冷剂流过一套货真价实的制冷回路。
cues.en: We have a lil’ baby compressor back here pumping refrigerant through an honest-to-goodness refrigeration circuit.

cues.zh: 它买的时候确实比那个蓝色的……玩意儿贵不少，
cues.en: Now, it did cost significantly more money to purchase than the blue... thing,

cues.zh: 但它也能装更多东西。
cues.en: but it can also hold a lot more stuff.

cues.zh: 甚至能装下那个蓝色冰箱。
cues.en: Including the blue fridge.

cues.zh: 按照国际公认的指标——“每美元能塞进多少罐La Croix”
cues.en: By the internationally recognized metric of “how many cans of La Croix can you shove in there per dollar”

cues.zh: 真冰箱完胜。
cues.en: the real fridge wins by a lot.

cues.zh: 轻松装33罐，稍微动点脑筋能装36罐，算下来每罐2.77美元。
cues.en: It’ll hold 33 cans easily, and 36 if you’re a little bit creative, which works out to $2.77 per can.

cues.zh: 而蓝色冰箱虽然只要30美元，却只能装六罐，也就是每罐5美元。
cues.en: And the blue fridge, despite only costing $30, only holds six cans so that’s $5 per can.

cues.zh: 但这并不是真正的问题。
cues.en: But that’s not the real issue.

cues.zh: 记住，蓝色冰箱一直耗电55瓦。
cues.en: Remember, the blue fridge uses 55 watts all the time.

cues.zh: 猜猜这东西耗多少电？
cues.en: Guess how much power this thing uses?

cues.zh: 一旦制冷回路稳定下来，它从插座取电在45到50瓦之间。
cues.en: Once the refrigeration circuit has stabilized, it pulls between 45 and 50 watts from the wall.

cues.zh: 我咨询了一些数学学者，他们向我确认，这个数字低于那个愚蠢的蓝色冰箱所耗的55瓦。
cues.en: I’ve consulted with some math scholars who have confirmed for me that that figure is less than the 55 watts the stupid blue fridge pulls.

cues.zh: 但这还不是全部！
cues.en: But that’s not all!

cues.zh: 这个，因为它是真正的冰箱，有恒温器来保持内部食物安全的温度！
cues.en: This, because it’s an actual refrigerator, has a thermostat to maintain food safe temperatures inside!

cues.zh: 这意味着它不会一直运行。
cues.en: And that means it doesn’t run all the time.

cues.zh: 我监测了它装满15罐已经冷藏过的饮料时的能耗，为了在三小时内保持它们凉爽，
cues.en: I monitored its energy use when loaded up with 15 already-chilled beverage cans, and to keep them cool over three hours,

cues.zh: 它只消耗了65瓦时，平均功耗为21.7瓦。
cues.en: it consumed just 65 watt-hours representing an average draw of 21.7 watts.

cues.zh: 顺便说一下，那次测试时房间温度高达78华氏度，挺热的。
cues.en: And, by the way, the room it was in during that test was a pretty warm 78 degrees.

cues.zh: 现在，电可不是免费的。
cues.en: Now, electricity isn’t free.

cues.zh: 所以我们来做个简单的成本比较。
cues.en: So let’s do a little cost comparison.

cues.zh: 蓝色冰箱持续消耗55瓦，每月将耗电39.6千瓦时。
cues.en: The blue fridge, with its constant 55 watt draw, will consume 39.6 kilowatt-hours per month.

cues.zh: 按照美国平均电价每千瓦时0.14美元计算，连续使用每月大约花费5.50美元。
cues.en: Going by the average cost of electricity in the US of $0.14 per kilowatt-hour, it will cost about $5.50 per month to use continuously.

cues.zh: 所以一年约66美元。
cues.en: So about $66 a year.

cues.zh: 另一方面，大得多的迷你冰箱持续消耗22瓦，一个月耗电15.8千瓦时，
cues.en: The much larger mini fridge, on the other hand, drawing 22 watts continuously will consume 15.8 kilowatt-hours in a month,

cues.zh: 每月花费2.21美元，也就是一年27美元。

cues.en: That may sound impossible, but the compressor is the only thing in here doing any work,

cues.zh: 它所做的就是用电动马达带动这个外壳里的一些泵送部件，给气体加压。
cues.en: and all it’s doing is using an electric motor to spin some pumpy parts inside this enclosure which pressurizes a gas.

cues.zh: 就这台冰箱而言，它 literally 就只做这一件事。
cues.en: In the case of this fridge, that’s literally the only thing it’s doing.

cues.zh: 其余所有部件都只是管道和管子，暴露在内部和外部的空气中。

cues.zh: 它压缩的气体叫做制冷剂。

cues.zh: 制冷剂是我们发现（有时是人工设计）的一类气体，
cues.en: Refrigerants are a category of gasses that we’ve discovered (or sometimes engineered)

cues.zh: 它们的压力和沸点之间有着非常有用的关系。
cues.en: that have really useful relationships between their pressure and their boiling point.

cues.zh: 这台冰箱和当今市场上的大多数冰箱一样，使用的是异丁烷，它在常压下是气体。
cues.en: This fridge, like most on the market today, uses isobutane which at atmospheric pressure is a gas.

cues.zh: 但如果把异丁烷加压到约80 PSI，它的沸点就会飙升到110华氏度。
cues.en: But if you pressurize isobutane to about 80 PSI, its boiling point shoots up to 110 degrees Fahrenheit.

cues.zh: 这比典型的室温高得多，
cues.en: That’s much hotter than typical room temperatures,

cues.zh: 所以如果你让这种高压气体流经暴露在环境空气中的一些管子，
cues.en: so if you feed that high pressure gas through some tubes that are exposed to ambient air,

cues.zh: 空气会把它冷却到无法再保持气态的程度，它就会自发凝结成液体。
cues.en: the air will cool it down to the point that it can’t be a gas anymore and it will spontaneously condense into a liquid.

cues.zh: 这个凝结过程会释放大量热能，这是因为一个叫做汽化潜热的东西，为了节省时间我现在就不展开讲了，
cues.en: That condensing action releases a ton of heat energy because of a thing called the latent heat of vaporization which to save time I am not getting into right now,

cues.zh: 但你可以在热成像相机中看到这些热量被释放出来。
cues.en: but you can see this heat being released in the thermal camera.

cues.en: You can even make out the tubes the refrigerant is traveling through just below the surface of the fridge’s outer skin.

cues.zh: 多亏了压缩机的泵送作用，制冷剂被主动推着流过这些管道。
cues.en: Thanks to the pumping action of the compressor, the refrigerant is actively pushed through those tubes.

cues.zh: 在入口处，它纯粹是高温气体（之所以热，是因为压缩机刚刚压缩过它），
cues.en: At the entrance it’s purely hot gas (and it’s hot because the compressor just compressed it),

cues.zh: 但随着它一路前行，它会散发热量并开始液化。
cues.en: but as it makes its way through it sheds heat energy and begins to liquify.

cues.zh: 等它到达管道末端时，一段液态制冷剂就已经聚集起来了。
cues.en: By the time it makes it to the end of the tube, a slug of liquid refrigerant will have bunched up.

cues.zh: 然后，这些液态制冷剂会经过一个限流装置，限制流体的流量。
cues.en: Then, that liquid refrigerant gets sent through a restriction which limits the volume of fluid flow.

cues.zh: 由于限流装置和压缩机的泵送作用，两侧之间维持着压力不平衡。
cues.en: Because of the restriction and the pumping action of the compressor, a pressure imbalance is maintained on either side.

cues.zh: 一旦液体通过，就会进入蒸发器，那里的压力非常低，
cues.en: And once the liquid makes it through it finds itself inside the evaporator where the pressure is very low,

cues.zh: 低到异丁烷的沸点骤降至约零下20华氏度。
cues.en: in fact so low that the boiling point of isobutane plummets to something like -20 degrees Fahrenheit.

cues.zh: 连冷冻室里的空气都比这暖和，这意味着有能量可以让制冷剂沸腾。
cues.en: Even the air inside a freezer is warmer than that, which means there’s energy available to boil the refrigerant.

cues.zh: 这使它吸收潜热能量，从而变得非常非常冷。
cues.en: That causes it to absorb latent heat energy which means it gets very, very cold.

cues.zh: 一旦制冷剂完全沸腾、再次变成气体，它就会回到压缩机，整个过程重新开始。
cues.en: Once the refrigerant has completely boiled away and becomes a gas once more, it finds itself back at the compressor and the whole thing starts over again.

cues.zh: 它压缩的气体叫做制冷剂。
cues.en: The gas it’s compressing is called a refrigerant.

cues.zh: 制冷剂是我们发现（有时是设计出来）的一类气体——
cues.en: Refrigerants are a category of gasses that we’ve discovered (or sometimes engineered) that —

cues.zh: 理解这一过程的关键在于，制冷剂通过沸腾吸走大量热能。
cues.en: Key to understanding this process is that the refrigerant, through boiling away, absorbs a lot of heat energy.

cues.zh: 这些热能随后储存在制冷剂中。
cues.en: That heat energy is then stored in the refrigerant.

cues.zh: 但当我们压缩它、使其冷凝回液态时，它就会释放出刚刚吸收的能量。
cues.en: But, when we compress it and it condenses back into a liquid, it releases the energy it had just absorbed.

cues.zh: 由于我们能控制这一过程发生的位置，就可以把热能从一个地方转移到另一个地方。
cues.en: Since we’re in control of where that happens, we can move heat energy from one place to another.

cues.zh: 以冰箱为例，我们把热量从冰箱内部抽出来，从而使内部降温，
cues.en: In the case of a fridge, we’re pumping the heat out of the fridge’s interior which cools it down

cues.zh: 然后再把这些热量释放到外面的空气中。
cues.en: and then releasing that heat to the outside air.

cues.zh: 而我们要做的，只是压缩一种气体并把它推送过一些管道。
cues.en: And the only thing we’re doing to make that happen is compress a gas and pushing it through some pipes.

cues.zh: 热量的转移全靠制冷剂自己完成。
cues.en: The refrigerant does the heat transfer stuff all on its own.

cues.zh: 这就是蒸汽压缩式热泵能搬运比机器自身消耗更多能量的原因。
cues.en: That is how a vapor-compression heat pump is able to move more energy than the machine itself consumes.

cues.zh: 与功耗相比的热量移动能力，这个指标被称为性能系数。
cues.en: The heat moving capacity compared to its power draw is a metric known as the coefficient of performance.

cues.zh: 现在，没有多少人会计算冰箱的COP，
cues.en: Now, not many people calculate the COP of a fridge,

cues.zh: 但如果我假设它的COP为3，那么我们得到的冷却功率就是输入功率的三倍。
cues.en: but if I assume it has a COP of 3 then we get a threefold increase in cooling power compared to input power.

cues.zh: 换句话说，这台冰箱运行时从墙上取用的45瓦功率，在蒸发器中产生了135瓦的冷却功率。
cues.en: In other words, the 45 watts of power this fridge pulls from the wall when it’s running generates 135 watts of cooling power in the evaporator.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们要费心用压缩机以及所有这些管道和杂七杂八的东西，
cues.en: That is why we bother with a compressor and all this piping and junk,

cues.zh: 它就是非常非常高效。
cues.en: it’s just really, really efficient.

cues.zh: 就像冷冻室里有余热可以抽出一样，室外空气中也有热量可以抓取。
cues.en: just as there’s heat to be pulled out of a freezer, there’s heat to be grabbed from the air outside.

cues.zh: 只要运行中的热泵COP大于1，相比用电热元件，我们就能获得一些免费的热量。
cues.en: And so long as the COP of an operating heat pump is over 1, we're getting some free heat compared to running an electric heating element.

cues.en: Peltier elements, because they move heat from one side to the other, are technically heat pumps.

cues.zh: 这意味着我们可以测量它们的性能系数。
cues.en: And that means we can measure their coefficient of performance.

cues.zh: 但这很难做，因为与蒸汽压缩式热泵不同，它的效率会随它对抗的温差而剧烈变化，
